The *Mālukyaputtattheragāthā* (Thag 16.5) is a poetic discourse in the *Theragāthā* collection of the Pali Canon, consisting of verses attributed to the elder Mālukyaputta [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into eight modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a primary canonical parallel in the *Mālukyaputtasutta* of the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35.95) [SuttaCentral]. This alignment is strongly confirmed by DharmaNexus, which records 48 matching segments between Thag 16.5 and SN 35, exhibiting near-total verbatim agreement across verses §0.4–24.6 and SN 35.95 §95.12.1–95.35.6 (similarity 0.99) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records internal Pali text reuse with the commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā*, and minor shared verse segments with neighboring poems in the collection, namely *Abhayattheragāthā* (Thag 1.98) and *Uttiyattheragāthā* (Thag 1.99) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus computes cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and several Tibetan translations, including the *Ratnacūḍaparipṛcchā* (D 91), the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D 287), and various *Prajñāpāramitā* texts [DharmaNexus].
